# tenarium_tenant_domain (Resource)

A custom hostname of a tenant. Publish the TXT record given by `txt_record_name` and `txt_record_value`, then set `verify = true` to prove ownership.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tenarium_tenant_domain" "app" {
  tenant_id = tenarium_tenant.acme.id
  hostname  = "app.acme.example"
  verify    = true
}

# Publish the challenge, e.g. with the AWS provider.
resource "aws_route53_record" "tenarium_challenge" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = tenarium_tenant_domain.app.txt_record_name
  type    = "TXT"
  ttl     = 60
  records = [tenarium_tenant_domain.app.txt_record_value]
}

variable "zone_id" {
  type = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hostname` (String) Fully qualified hostname, e.g. `app.example.com`. Changing it replaces the domain.
- `tenant_id` (String) ID (or slug) of the tenant. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `verify` (Boolean) When true, Terraform asks the server to verify the TXT record. If the record is not visible yet, apply succeeds with a warning and the next plan retries. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<tenant_id>/<hostname>`.
- `txt_record_name` (String) Name of the TXT record to publish.
- `txt_record_value` (String) Value of the TXT record to publish.
- `verification_token` (String) Verification token.
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether ownership has been verified.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import tenarium_tenant_domain.app <tenant_id>/app.acme.example
```
